title: Generalized Ballot Sequences
content:
**kCountedSequence** defines the set of vote sequences for the k-fold ballot problem:
- Exactly `a` votes for candidate A (value +1)
- Exactly `b` votes for candidate B (value $-k$)
- All elements are either 1 or $-k$

When $k = 1$, this is exactly Mathlib's `countedSequence`.
mathContext: \{l \mid l.\text{count}(1) = a \wedge l.\text{count}(-k) = b \wedge \forall x \in l, x = 1 \vee x = -k\}

title: Sum Identity for Binary Lists
content:
For any list with only 1 and $-k$ values, the sum equals count(1) - k * count(-k). This is the core algebraic identity connecting list sums to element counts.

Proved by induction on the list, using `List.count_cons` to track how counts change.

title: Permutation Characterization
content:
Every element of kCountedSequence is a permutation of the canonical witness `replicate a 1 ++ replicate b (-k)`. This is proved using `List.perm_iff_count` - two lists are permutations iff they have the same count for every element.

This characterization immediately gives finiteness: the set of permutations of a finite list is finite.

title: Classical Reduction (k = 1)
content:
When $k = 1$, our generalized definition exactly matches Mathlib's `Ballot.countedSequence`. The proof is remarkably clean: just `simpa` to convert $-(1 : \mathbb{Z})$ to $-1$.

This validates our generalization against the established formalization.

title: Rotation Preserves Ballot Sequences
content: Cyclic rotation of a ballot sequence produces another ballot sequence. The key insight: rotation = `drop i ++ take i`, and counts are additive over append. Using `congr_arg` on the identity `take i l ++ drop i l = l`, we get that drop-then-take and take-then-drop have the same combined counts.

title: Prefix Sum Relation for Rotations
content:
The key structural lemma for the cycle lemma. For rotation starting at position $i$, the prefix sum at position $j$ is:

- **Non-wrapping** ($i + j \leq n$): $\text{prefixSum}(i+j) - \text{prefixSum}(i)$
- **Wrapping** ($i + j > n$): $\text{prefixSum}(i+j-n) + S - \text{prefixSum}(i)$

where $S$ is the total sum. This uses helper lemmas `sum_drop_eq` and `take_drop_sum`.

title: The Cycle Lemma (Dvoretzky-Motzkin)
content:
**Statement**: For a sequence of integers with positive sum $S$ and length $n$, exactly $S$ of the $n$ cyclic rotations have all positive prefix sums.

**Proof Strategy** (not yet formalized): Use the rightmost minimum argument. Among the $2n$ prefix sums of the doubled sequence, each window of $n$ has exactly $S$ positions where a new running minimum is achieved. These correspond to good starting positions.

This is the fundamental counting tool for the generalized ballot problem.
mathContext: $|\{i : 0 \leq i < n, \text{rotation } i \text{ has all positive prefix sums}\}| = S$
